source: Ferrando, Obeso, Rajamanoharan, Nanda (2025, ICLR) Do I know this entity? Knowledge awareness and hallucinations in language models
finding: Sparse-autoencoder directions inside Gemma 2 separate known from unknown entities (players, movies, songs, cities). This is a built-in recognition signal. Steering it flips refusal: the model refuses about known entities or answers about unknown ones.
numbers: Gemma 2 2B and 9B; Llama 3.1 8B replicated in an appendix. Pushing the unknown-entity latent gives almost 100% refusal across all four entity types in Gemma 2 2B. Pushing the known-entity latent slightly lowers refusal.
quote: these directions have a causal effect on the chat model's refusal behavior
limits: Mechanistic work on small open models. No test of the signal as a one-reason cue in a paired comparison. Models are biased toward Yes for unknown entities.
agent_relevance: An LLM has a recognition-like signal (entity known or not). It is a real internal cue, but we cannot read it through an API; only behavioural proxies are available.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Large models can judge whether their own sample is true (P(True)) and can be trained to predict P(IK), the chance they know the answer, before answering. P(IK) partly generalises across tasks but is poorly calibrated on new tasks. Showing the model many of its own samples improves self-evaluation, like self-consistency.
numbers: AUROC separates known from unknown questions. k-shot self-evaluation mainly improves calibration, not AUROC. Exact AUROCs are in figures and were not read.
quote: models struggle with calibration of P(IK) on new tasks
limits: Trained P(IK) probe, not a zero-shot prompt. 2022 models.
agent_relevance: Familiarity (P(IK)) is a learnable single cue with domain-dependent calibration, the same shape as the human 54% vs 89% recognition split.

source: Kossen et al. (2024) Semantic entropy probes: robust and cheap hallucination detection in LLMs
finding: Semantic entropy (disagreement in meaning across several sampled answers) costs 5 to 10 times more compute. A linear probe on the hidden states of one generation approximates it at almost no cost. It can even be predicted before any token is generated.
numbers: AUROC for predicting binarised semantic entropy reaches 0.7 to 0.95 depending on model, task and layer; slightly lower before generation. Probes generalise out of distribution better than accuracy probes.
quote: reducing the overhead of semantic uncertainty quantification to almost zero
limits: White-box (needs hidden states). Sampling-based semantic entropy is the black-box version.
agent_relevance: Self-consistency across samples is a costly but valid familiarity cue. A pre-generation probe would be the cheap S0 gate signal if we ever get model internals.

source: Anon. (2026) Do LLMs know what they know? Measuring metacognitive efficiency with signal detection theory
finding: The confidence signal (token log-probability) tracks correctness differently by model and by domain. Calibration metrics hide this. Knowing more does not mean confidence is more informative.
numbers: 4 LLMs, 224,000 factual QA trials. Metacognitive information differs by a factor of 1.98 across models. Rank correlation with accuracy -0.80 on TriviaQA and +0.00 on Natural Questions. Weakest in Science and Technology for every model. Gain from confidence-based abstention tracked metacognitive information exactly (rho +1.00).
limits: Preprint, 7-9B open models, factual QA only, log-prob confidence.
agent_relevance: Cue validity of confidence depends on domain, like recognition validity in humans. Measure it per task class before using it as a gate.

source: Davis-Stober, Dana, Budescu (2010) Why recognition is rational: optimality results on single-variable decision rules. Judgment and Decision Making 5(4)
finding: Peer-reviewed theory in JDM: single-variable rules such as the recognition heuristic can be optimal under a linear model. It gives conditions where one cue beats a full regression. Page read through a fetch-tool summary, not the full PDF.
numbers: Empirical part is a 25-subject German-cities recognition study (83 cities, 9 binary cues). No 20-data-set accuracy table.
quote: outperform standard regression models until samples become very large
limits: Theory; relies on linear-model assumptions. Czerlinski 1999 is not cited there.
agent_relevance: Gives a formal test for when a single-cue gate should beat a many-cue rule: small samples, high cue validity.

source: Chen et al. (2024/2025) Do NOT think that much for 2+3=? On the overthinking of o1-like LLMs
finding: o1-like models burn many tokens on trivial questions, and later solution rounds add little accuracy. The first round is already right in most correct cases. Overthinking is worse on easy items.
numbers: On 'what is 2 plus 3?' o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional models. In more than 92% of correct cases the first solution round was already correct, and the first round is under 60% of tokens. Table 1: QwQ-32B-Preview 3.5 solutions and 741.8 tokens on ASDIV vs 1.0 solution and 166.4 tokens for Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct.
quote: In more than 92% of cases, the initial round of solutions produces the correct answer.
limits: Math sets only (ASDIV, GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, AIME). The fix is a trained self-training method. Token counts, not latency.
agent_relevance: Real cost of the many-step mode vs direct answer: roughly 5 times the tokens or more on easy items. That is the price of a false 'think' on easy items and the saving from a correct skip.

source: Thinkless: LLM learns when to think (2025)
finding: A 1.5B model trained with RL to choose a short or long reasoning mode per query via control tokens. It routes easy queries to short mode and keeps long mode on hard ones (AIME). This is a learned mode gate.
numbers: Cuts long-chain thinking by 50% to 90% on Minerva Algebra, MATH-500 and GSM8K. Reasoning models emit 5 to 20 times more tokens than standard models (their words). GSM8K Pass@1 stays about 0.82 to 0.86 in Table 1; the row alignment in the extracted text is garbled, so read this as approximate.
quote: Thinkless reduces the usage of long-chain thinking by 50% 90%
limits: Trained router on a distilled 1.5B model, not a prompted gate. Table columns hard to read from text.
agent_relevance: A trained gate can keep accuracy while skipping most thinking, which supports K13. Gap 7 is only partly answered: this is a learned router, not an FFT built from data, and there is no head-to-head with prompted routing.

source: Fan et al. (2025) Missing premise exacerbates overthinking: are reasoning models losing critical thinking skill?
finding: Independent group. Reasoning models write far longer answers on ill-posed questions with a missing premise and rarely abstain. Non-reasoning models answer short and spot the problem. Reasoning models often suspect the problem early but do not act on it.
numbers: Datasets MiP-SVAMP, MiP-GSM8K (582 items), MiP-MATH and others. Non-reasoning models give similar length for well-posed and ill-posed questions; reasoning models give much longer ones. Exact per-model lengths are in a figure and were not extracted.
quote: they typically fail to act on those suspicions
limits: Math word problems. GPT-4o was used to judge steps and abstention. Not the same items or design as Bogdan 2026.
agent_relevance: Partial independent support for K10: longer reasoning on unanswerable items is a known failure of reasoning models, so a gate should send indeterminate items to a short check, not a long chain.

source: Kirichenko, Ibrahim, Chaudhuri, Bell (2025) AbstentionBench: reasoning LLMs fail on unanswerable questions
finding: Large benchmark from a separate lab. Reasoning fine-tuning lowers abstention. A bigger reasoning token budget raises accuracy on reasoning tasks but generally lowers abstention further. A tailored system prompt helps but does not fix it.
numbers: 20 datasets, over 35k unanswerable questions, 20 frontier LLMs. Abstention recall drops 24% on average for DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama 70B and s1.1 32B vs their instruct counterparts. Budget sweeps were run on those two models.
quote: reasoning fine-tuning degrades abstention (by 24% on average)
limits: Abstention is scored by an LLM judge (judge identity not verified here). It measures abstention, not Bogdan's indeterminate items. The comparison is reasoning-tuned vs instruct, not CoT length alone.
agent_relevance: Closes much of gap 2 in direction: a second, larger, independent source says more reasoning hurts on unanswerable items. Frontier Claude and GPT models were not isolated in the budget sweep.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large language models can be easily distracted by irrelevant context (GSM-IC)
finding: Adding irrelevant sentences to math problems sharply cuts accuracy under all prompting techniques. Self-consistency and an instruction to ignore irrelevant information help.
numbers: Built from 1,000 GSM8K problems. Of the problems the baseline solves, no more than 18% stay solved across all kinds of irrelevant context. Fewer than 30% of base problems are consistently solved after distractors (macro accuracy). Models code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003.
quote: model performance is dramatically decreased when irrelevant information is included
limits: 2022 models. Distractors are irrelevant, not low-validity cues, and there is no ordering by validity.
agent_relevance: Indirect support for cue limiting: full-information prompts are not free. It does not show that a top-k validity-ordered prompt wins, so gap 1 stays open.

source: Vacareanu et al. (2024, COLM) From words to numbers: your LLM is secretly a capable regressor when given in-context examples
finding: Large LLMs learn numeric linear and non-linear regression from in-context examples alone. So LLMs can pick up cue weights from a handful of cases. They do it as regression, not as take-the-best.
numbers: 50 in-context (x,y) tuples; 12 LLMs. Claude 3 Opus and GPT-4 rank above Random Forest, Gradient Boosting and KNN on the linear sets. Claude 3 beats AdaBoost, SVM, RF, KNN and GB on Friedman #2 and approaches linear regression on a 1-of-2 informative-variable set.
quote: Claude 3 approaches the performance of a Linear Regression model
limits: Numeric inputs, synthetic tasks, 50 exemplars. No binary-cue paired-comparison task and no test against take-the-best.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 partly answered: in-context weight learning works at 50 examples, so cue validities could be estimated in context. Whether LLMs default to compensatory weighting on binary cues is untested.

source: Suri, Slater, Ziaee, Nguyen (2023) Do large language models show decision heuristics similar to humans? A case study using GPT-3.5
finding: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) showed anchoring, representativeness and availability effects, a framing effect and an endowment effect, and human participants showed similar effects on the same prompts. These are heuristics-and-biases, not the adaptive toolbox. Later journal publication is recalled, not verified from the file.
numbers: Four studies with matched human samples; sample sizes not extracted.
quote: ChatGPT was influenced by random anchors in making estimates
limits: One model, 2023. Does not test take-the-best, recognition or fast-and-frugal trees.
agent_relevance: For gap 9: the LLM work I could open is heuristics-and-biases, not ecological rationality.

source: Hutchinson & Gigerenzer (2005) Simple heuristics and rules of thumb: where psychologists and behavioural biologists might meet. Behavioural Processes
finding: Text read. Take-the-best on 83 German cities is about equal to or better than multiple regression in cross-validation. With small learning samples it nearly always beats C4.5 and CART. The regression comparison holds in 19 other real-world tasks (Czerlinski et al. 1999). Fig 1 averages 1000 random learning sets.
numbers: Percentages are only in a figure. The text gives 20 data sets in total and says many of the 20 environments tend toward non-compensatory cue structures.
quote: the comparison against multiple regression holds in 19 other such real-world comparison tasks
limits: Secondhand for Czerlinski; no percentages in the text. Written by the same camp.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: confirms the claim and its scope but not the exact 20-set percentages.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026-11-01) Take-the-best heuristic, citing Czerlinski, Goldstein, Gigerenzer (1999)
finding: Secondary page. On the 83-city data, out of sample over 10,000 random splits: take-the-best 72.2%, regression 71.9%, unit-weight (tallying) 71.4%. In sample about 74% for all three; that line is tagged 'citation needed'.
numbers: Out of sample: TTB 72.2, regression 71.9, tallying 71.4 (city data only, not the 20-set average). In sample: 74.3 regression, 74.2 TTB, 74.1 unit weight.
quote: regression had on average 71.9% correct, Take-the-best had 72.2% correct
limits: Wikipedia, not the 1999 chapter. The figure is for one data set, so it is not the 20-data-set result. Treat as unverified.
agent_relevance: Margins on the founding example are tiny (under 1 point). The edge is parity at lower cost, not a big accuracy win.

source: Negative search: LLMs on take-the-best, recognition heuristic, fast-and-frugal trees, adaptive toolbox (arXiv API queries, 2026-11-01)
finding: Queries combining take-the-best, recognition heuristic, fast-and-frugal, adaptive toolbox, less-is-more, lexicographic/compensatory with language model or LLM returned no paper that runs the founding paradigms on an LLM. Only hits: Bogdan 2606.15877 and two Jagadish ecological-prior papers (2402.01821, 2509.00116).
limits: arXiv only. The WebSearch quota ran out before peer-reviewed venues could be searched. A Frontiers in AI 2025 perspective (frai.2025.1592399) appeared in a snippet only.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1, 6 and 7 are unstudied in the literature we can reach; we would have to run them ourselves.

source: Negative search: Rieskamp & Otto (2006) strategy-selection-learning paradigm on LLMs
finding: No LLM study of strategy-selection learning (feedback-driven switching between take-the-best and weighted additive) was found by arXiv queries on strategy selection, lexicographic vs compensatory, and multi-attribute choice heuristics.
limits: Coverage limited to arXiv. Cognitive-science venues (CogSci proceedings, Cognition, Psychological Review) were not searched because the WebSearch quota ran out.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 stays open for the adaptive-strategy part.
